note: Both sets cover the same core facts (solar altitude 50°, window azimuth 0, the louver spacing algorithm and its D*1.2 simplification, 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, truncated isosceles triangle profile, powder-coated finish, 25° structural bend) and both are heavily padded with duplicate restatements of the same facts under slightly different entity/attribute names. Set A repeats three facts twice each (spacing formula, louver shape, bend angle), while Set B repeats four (bend angle, finish, spacing algorithm, shape) and additionally misattributes the 'optimal solar illumination' outcome to the powder-coated finish alone, whereas the page credits the screen's transparency and finish together. Set A is therefore marginally cleaner, with one fewer duplicate pair and no misbound quote, though neither set captures the proportional reduction of louver spacing based on average profile widths.
remarks: Both sets are dominated by near-duplicate claims (same value/quote restated under 'louver' vs 'Harvest Shade Screen louver', and 'shape' vs 'tapered into...', and 'spacing formula' vs 'spacing simplified formula'), which inflates apparent coverage without adding facts. Both also omit the stated design adjustment that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths, and neither notes that the 1:1 ratio provided optimal insulation from direct radiant heat gain. Set A's condition string 'along the louver longit' is a truncated quote fragment.
